newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX index opens at record bourse high.
newsitem.headline: German DAX index opens at record bourse high.

text.p: The German DAX index of 30 leading shares opened floor trade at a record high on Friday, driven by gains in bond prices and by the Dow Jones index which ended above 6,200 points for first time.

The DAX raced up 30.27 points, or over one percent, to 2,743.49 by 1010 GMT, jumping over the previous high of 2739.26 points reached on October 18. The index then slipped back slightly to 2,741.16 points.

Meanwhile shares in dialysis group Fresenius Medical Care dropped over one percent against the firmer market trend, falling two marks to 137 marks, after the company reported nine month sales of $2.3 billion against $2.1 billion a year previously.
Diversified industrial group Viag AG gained almost two percent, or 11.50 marks to 589.50 marks, after the firm said nine month group sales were unchanged at about 32 billion marks.
The company also said it expected 1996 group pretax profit to be at least as high as in 1995.

But shares in Viag subsidiary, speciality chemicals group SKW Trostberg, fell almost nine percent to hit a low of 41 marks, before recovering somewhat to stand down 2.42 marks at 42.50 marks, despite Viag saying sales increased at the unit.

The main selling on the stock came after BHF bank cut its recommendations on the firm to a "hold" from a "buy" and reduced its earnings per share estimates, saying the firm's results had been "slightly disappointing."

Car maker Volkswagen stocks were unchanged, but weaker than the rest of the market, after a newspaper reported that VW production chief Jose Ignacio Lopez and three others could be charged soon for alleged industial espionage.
The German Prosecutors office said it could not confirm that Lopez would be charged in November, but said it would decide by the end of the year whether to charge him.
Shares in Dresdner Bank AG reacted positively to news that the bank planned to merge its global funds businesses. Dresdner was up over three percent, or 1.25 marks at 42.75 marks.
